findings.failureScenario: A UI language is declared three times by hand: the language_table! entries (Locale::ALL order: ... Pt-BR, Es, De, Ru, Fr, Uk), LANGUAGE_COMMANDS (order: ... Pt-BR, Fr, Es, De, Ru, Uk) and language_from_command. The copies have already diverged in order: Settings > Language lists French after Russian (Locale::ALL), while Edit > Language lists it right after Portuguese (LANGUAGE_COMMANDS registry order). Adding a language means editing all three sites in step, and the coverage test only checks membership, not order.
findings.action: Generate LANGUAGE_COMMANDS and language_from_command from Locale::ALL (e.g. a command-id column in language_table!), so the menu, Settings and control channel share one ordered source.

findings.failureScenario: UI commands are a string table (UI_COMMANDS, 158 ids) whose behaviour lives in a single ~1,525-line match in run_ui_command, with enabled state in a separate string match (ui_enabled) and checked/live-label state in menubar.rs. Nothing ties the table to the handlers at compile time: an id added to UI_COMMANDS but missed or misspelled in run_ui_command falls through `_ => return None` to the engine and fails as an unknown command at runtime, and menu enablement defaults to `true` for any id ui_enabled does not name. All 158 current ids are handled today (checked), so this is a change-risk/shotgun-surgery finding, not a live break.
findings.action: Split run_ui_command by command family (view/panel/dialog/file/app) and add a test that every UI_COMMANDS id resolves to Some(..) in run_ui_command, or move to a typed command enum that carries label, shortcut, handler and enablement together.

findings.failureScenario: logic_inner calls panels::faces::pump twice in the same frame (after slideshow_tick and again after model_setup::pump). The second call's faces.pump engine step is mostly suppressed by faces_next_pump, but watch_downloads is not gated: while a face-model download is watched, the engine command faces.models.downloads is executed twice per frame, and input-time bookkeeping runs twice. Duplicate orchestration of one subsystem in the per-frame loop.
findings.action: Remove one of the two calls (keep a single per-frame faces pump in logic_inner).
